objects.abstract: OAuth provides a method for clients to access server resources on behalf of a resource owner (such as a different client or an end-user).  It also provides a process for end-users to authorize third-party access to their server resources without sharing their credentials (typically, a username and password pair), using user-agent redirections.  This document is not an Internet Standards Track specification; it is published for informational purposes.
objects.name: rfc5849
objects.title: The OAuth 1.0 Protocol

objects.abstract: The OAuth 2.0 authorization framework enables a third-party application to obtain limited access to an HTTP service, either on behalf of a resource owner by orchestrating an approval interaction between the resource owner and the HTTP service, or by allowing the third-party application to obtain access on its own behalf.  This specification replaces and obsoletes the OAuth 1.0 protocol described in RFC 5849. [STANDARDS-TRACK]
objects.name: rfc6749
objects.title: The OAuth 2.0 Authorization Framework
